# Fatality Analysis Reporting System: agent index

A census of fatal motor vehicle crashes in the 50 States, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico since 1975, coded from police reports and other records. Not a survey: there are no questions, and "unknown" means the records didn't say.

Publisher: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), National Center for Statistics and Analysis. Dataset id: `fars`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.nhtsa.gov/research-data/fatality-analysis-reporting-system-fars. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the data year.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves; forms | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span; a gap between runs (`1972-1985,1987-2024`) means the variable wasn't available in the waves between, even though the release has them. The release's waves are: `2024`: 2024. `forms A,C` lists every form the variable was on in any wave; the JSONL `availability` gives wave by form. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

Read `SKILL.md` before answering a question from these files.
